refuter_findings.location: Statement, last sentence ("Consequently μ is coadjoint equivariant if and only if c = 0"), and step 4.1
refuter_findings.evidence: The equivalence is asserted for an arbitrary Lie group G; only M is assumed connected. Counterexample (checked numerically): G = R ⋊ Z/2 (disconnected), g = R·e abelian, M = T*R = R², ω = dq∧dp, action (t,ε)·(q,p) = (εq + t, εp) (the Z/2-part is the cotangent lift of q ↦ −q, hence symplectic), and μ(q,p) = (p + c)e* with c ≠ 0. Then ξ_M = −ξ ∂_q and dμ^ξ = ξ dp = −ι_{ξ_M}ω, so μ satisfies the component equations, and c(ξ,η) = {μ^ξ,μ^η} − μ^{[ξ,η]} = 0 identically because the Lie algebra is abelian and {ξp + c′, ηp + c″} = 0. But μ is not coadjoint equivariant: for s = (0,−1), μ(s·(q,p)) = −p + c while s·μ(q,p) = −(p + c) = −p − c, and these differ whenever c ≠ 0. So c = 0 does not imply equivariance. The item's own cited dependency, [[prop-equivariance-is-equivalent-to-the-moment-map-poisson-bracket-identity]], states the correct qualification: "For a general group the bracket identity is equivalent to equivariance under the identity component G⁰, and equivariance under all of G requires in addition equivariance under one representative of each coset of G/G⁰." The Statement (and step 4.1) drops the connectedness of G.

refuter_findings.location: Definition, paragraph "The integers dim t_0 and dim a_0 are invariants of the conjugacy class of h_0"
refuter_findings.evidence: The inclusion α(t_0) ⊆ t_0′ is derived from the remark that "a subspace on which B is negative definite has zero intersection with a_0′ and hence dimension at most dim t_0′". That reasoning yields only dim α(t_0) ≤ dim t_0′ (and, symmetrically, dim α(a_0) ≤ dim a_0′); a B-negative-definite subspace of h_0′ of the full dimension dim t_0′ need not be contained in t_0′: in h_0′ = span{t,a} with B(t,t) = −1, B(a,a) = 1, the line span{t + a/2} is B-negative-definite of dimension dim t_0′ = 1 yet is not contained in t_0′. The claim itself is true (positive definiteness of B_{θ′} forces θ′X = X for X ∈ t_0′\{0} and θ′X = −X for X ∈ a_0′\{0}, so θ and θ′ agree on h_0′ and α(t_0) = t_0′); only the stated justification fails to license the inclusion, and the repair is immediate.

refuter_findings.location: Statement, penultimate sentence: "the form being ω_α ⊕ β-product on the left"
refuter_findings.evidence: The Statement reads "… is a symplectomorphism onto the reduced product, the form being ω_α ⊕ β-product on the left and the reduced form on the right." Here β is a regular value of μ_N, i.e. a covector in h*, not a two-form, so "ω_α ⊕ β" is not a well-typed expression; the intended object, and the one actually used in step 3.1 ("the pullback of ω_α ⊕ ω_β"), is ω_α ⊕ ω_β.
